text: [playful, curious documentary narrator, bright energy] What if every human on Earth jumped at the same time? First, we'd all have to meet up. Eight billion people, packed shoulder to shoulder, fit inside an area the size of one small American state. [pause] On the count of three... jump. Together, we weigh around five hundred billion kilograms. That sounds enormous. But Earth is more than ten trillion times heavier. So when we push off, the planet moves less than a thousandth of the width of an atom. Then we land. A roar louder than any stadium, heard for kilometres around... and the ground barely notices. [leaning in] The real problem is what comes next. Eight billion people, one tiny state, a handful of roads and a single airport. Getting everyone home would take months, and the food and water would run out within days. [building tension] The jump was easy. Leaving is the disaster. So... would you jump?
